mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 500K units signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are not significantly below baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the trigger does not precede statistically significant negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered episodes compared to baseline (p > 0.05), or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals a liquidity trap, where further monetary easing fails to stimulate demand, resulting in flat or negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede statistically significant negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth above 5% for three months) combined with a simultaneous decline in consumer spending (GDPC1 growth below 1%) signals a savings glut that depresses consumption-driven equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 5% for 3 months AND GDPC1 growth < 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the joint trigger does not precede statistically significant negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede statistically significant positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which increases earnings visibility and supports higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered episodes compared to baseline (p > 0.05), or the trigger does not precede positive returns in more than 60% of cases.
